'''Sela''' is a goatherd from the outermost valleys of [[the Light Heights]] — too poor and too far away for anyone to teach her the house's names for the dead — who ''heard'': loudly, publicly, irresistibly.

In a winter when sheep-sickness took her valley, she sat beside a recently dead woman she barely knew and heard — not words, a direction. She told the village to move the herd over the northern pass, against all reason, the day before a landslide buried the old pastures. The village lived. She was not celebrated; she was feared. It was the first thing she learned about hearing: no one wants to sit beside the one who does it.

She speaks rarely and briefly, with a directness that silences learned men — she never learned the rhetoric, so she says only what she hears, and that is exactly why people believe her. She always sits facing an opening: a door, a window, the mouth of the valley.

{{Quote|I didn't ask to hear. I don't ask you to follow.|Sela}}

The people already follow her. [[Brother Tomas]] must soon test her.
